displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that reflective Christianity may remain credible when its philosophical, experiential, historical, and defeater-control considerations are treated as mutually constraining components of a modest cumulative case rather than independent demonstrations.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the live presentation by integrating its strongest considerations into one explicitly modest cumulative thesis.

premises.text: Moral value can provide a nonarbitrary but incomplete constraint upon divine motivation: embodied conscious communities realize agency, relationship, responsibility, creativity, and vulnerability-dependent virtues that form a recognizable package of interconnected goods.

novelty.explanation: This strengthens the moral-motivation proposal while acknowledging and answering the alternative-possibilities objection.

premises.text: Fine-tuning should be framed conditionally and transparently: natural and psychophysical laws may enter the comparison only where their background status is independently justified, while any unexplained lawful structure remains part of the total evidence.

novelty.explanation: This corrects the evidential-partition weakness by refusing to background disputed laws without independent justification.

premises.text: Direct religious experience may confer prima facie first-person warrant, but awareness of incompatible experiences creates a defeater that must be answered through comparative coherence, moral consequences, communal checking, and fit with independent evidence.

novelty.explanation: This preserves experiential warrant while directly incorporating the rival-experience discrimination burden.

premises.text: Resurrection has explanatory force only if the relevant historical data are independently supported and the full miraculous hypothesis explains them more simply and coherently than the complete naturalistic sequence, not merely isolated hallucination proposals.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the comparison by requiring complete hypothesis-level evaluation and independent support for the data.

premises.text: Suffering, religious confusion, moral failure, and informed dissent are genuine counterevidence; epistemic limitation may reduce particular likelihood judgments only when independently motivated and cannot erase these observations wholesale.

novelty.explanation: This limits the skeptical-theist defense and integrates concessions that the live cumulative case left insufficiently explicit.

conclusion.text: Accordingly, Christianity may be held as a reasonable but revisable cumulative judgment if its positive considerations retain comparative force after the acknowledged counterevidence and no single component is asked to carry demonstrative weight.

novelty.explanation: This extends the live confidence-limiting position into a proportionate cumulative conclusion.

newArguments.title: Interlocking explanatory constraints
newArguments.text: A cumulative Christian case improves when its components constrain one another instead of merely adding weak probabilities. The moral account of divine purpose should predict the broad kind of world invoked by fine-tuning; the claimed revelation should clarify that purpose; religious experience should cohere with the revelation; and resurrection evidence should connect the historical claim to the same theological character. Failure of any linkage reduces the whole case, but successful cross-constraint is more informative than a list of unrelated considerations because fewer auxiliary assumptions are available to rescue each component separately.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new coherence test requiring positive arguments to generate reciprocal predictions rather than merely accumulate.

newArguments.title: Costly corrigibility as evidence
newArguments.text: Reflective Christianity can treat institutional mechanisms of confession, repentance, public correction, and protection of dissenters as testable implications of its moral claims. The relevant prediction is not that Christians never fail, but that communities seriously governed by the tradition should become more capable of detecting, admitting, and repairing wrongdoing than comparable communities lacking those mechanisms. This reframing answers crude perfection comparisons while retaining empirical risk: persistent concealment, retaliation, or resistance to correction would count against the claimed transformative pattern rather than being insulated by appeals to imperfect believers.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a measurable institutional prediction distinct from the participant's general appeal to Christian credibility.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that skeptical atheism is supported when Christianity's positive considerations lack stable comparative predictions while suffering, religious contingency, informed disagreement, and moral outcomes form convergent evidence against its specified divine and revelatory claims.

novelty.explanation: This extends the principal skeptical moves into one proportionate cumulative thesis about comparative expectations.

premises.text: A hypothesis gains support from an observation only relative to alternatives, so identifying a possible divine reason for a world, text, experience, or miracle does not establish that the observation is appreciably expected under Christianity.

novelty.explanation: This generalizes the comparative-likelihood objection across several positive Christian arguments.

premises.text: Naturalistic resurrection proposals must be assessed as complete causal models with historically grounded rates and dependencies; their skeptical value comes from adequate explanatory competition, not from the bare logical possibility of each component.

novelty.explanation: This corrects the live sequence's compressed warrant by requiring evidence for mechanisms and their joint operation.

premises.text: Apparently preventable suffering and unequal access to revelation have evidential force because specified Christian commitments generate expectations about divine goodness and communication, although their weight depends upon carefully defined theological models.

novelty.explanation: This preserves the strongest world-evidence arguments while making their model dependence explicit.

premises.text: Informed dissent primarily constrains confidence rather than independently proving atheism, but persistent division across relevant expertise is especially significant when the proposed evidence is claimed to be publicly accessible and cumulatively powerful.

novelty.explanation: This sharpens the bounded social-epistemic conclusion and connects it to public-evidence claims.

premises.text: Christian transformation claims should generate preregistered, risk-bearing predictions involving defined populations, behaviors, time horizons, and comparison groups, with safeguards against explaining every unfavorable result through auxiliary doctrines.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the original observational test by specifying the design features needed for meaningful evaluation.

conclusion.text: Therefore, a skeptical conclusion is warranted to the extent that Christianity's positive evidence remains underdetermined and its specified expectations fit the observed world less well than relevant naturalistic alternatives, while confidence remains open to better evidence.

novelty.explanation: This extends the cumulative skeptical route while keeping the conclusion conditional and revisable.

newArguments.title: Predictive compression test
newArguments.text: Compare Christianity and naturalism by how economically each accounts for the entire evidence set after auxiliary assumptions are counted. A Christian model that separately invokes unknown divine reasons for fine-tuning, hidden goods for suffering, noncoercion for confusion, human freedom for moral failure, and mystery for dissent may fit each datum but lose predictive compression. The skeptical claim is not that auxiliary explanations are automatically false; it is that a model requiring many independently adjustable explanations risks accommodating almost any outcome and therefore yields less discriminating expectation than its verbal scope suggests.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new model-complexity argument evaluating the cumulative cost of independently adjustable theological auxiliaries.

newArguments.title: Revelation transmission benchmark
newArguments.text: A benevolent revealer need not eliminate freedom or cultural diversity to improve information transmission. Christianity can therefore be compared with ordinary robust communication systems: important messages are repeated through independent channels, central content survives foreseeable corruption, sincere inquirers receive accessible clarification, and consequential misunderstandings trigger correction. Geographic dependence, prolonged doctrinal fragmentation, and reliance upon disputed historical testimony become evidentially relevant when they resemble unmanaged human transmission more than a fault-tolerant revelatory process. This benchmark remains defeasible because a theological account may justify particular tradeoffs, but it makes those tradeoffs explicit and comparatively assessable.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a fault-tolerant communication benchmark for evaluating revelation without assuming perfect uniformity.
